title: Claims Desk Basis Note: Temporary Credits and the Close of a Personal Checking Claim
content:
**When a temporary credit is owed.** A temporary credit is owed on a Personal Checking claim that is still submitted once the tier's number of business days has passed after the owner gave notice. Business days are Monday through Friday excluding Federal Reserve holidays; count business days with the first business day after the notice date as day 1; the credit is due when the frozen date is on or after the business day that ends the count. Where the account was opened fewer than the tier's new-account period of calendar days before the notice date, the tier's longer new-account deadline in business days governs instead.

**Conditions.**

1. Only a claim whose status is submitted can receive a temporary credit.
2. Each claim receives at most one temporary credit, the claim itself identifying it.
3. A temporary credit may be reversed only when the claim's status is resolved in the bank's favour or withdrawn, and the reversal is recorded against the temporary credit it reverses.
4. Where the claim is resolved in the owner's favour the temporary credit becomes final with no further entry, and every charge for an item paid into overdraft that was recorded against the disputed item is refunded on the finally decided claim ground.

**Clauses no longer in force.** Two clauses of this basis have been superseded by the current charter and are recorded here only so that no reader applies them: the clause setting the temporary credit at the amount the owner claimed, capped at the amount of the disputed item, is **no longer in force**; and the clause requiring the reversal to be taken for the whole of the temporary credit is **no longer in force**. Neither may be used to work out what a temporary credit or a reversal comes to. The status conditions, the one-credit rule, the deadlines and the treatment of a claim decided in the owner's favour all stand.

**Boundary case (hypothetical).** On a tier whose ordinary deadline is 10 business days, notice given on a Monday that is not a holiday makes Tuesday day 1; the credit is due on the tenth business day so counted, and stays due on every later day while the claim is still submitted. Where the account was 12 calendar days old at notice, the 20-business-day deadline governs instead.

superseded_clauses: The provisional credit amount is the dispute's claimed_amount, but never more than the disputed item's amount.
